You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test case tests element-by-element multiplication (ebeMultiply) of two vectors of the same type. The current bug report indicates that OpenMapRealVector.ebeMultiply returns wrong values when one element of the other vector is NaN or infinity. 

Inspecting the source for OpenMapRealVector.ebeMultiply, we see the following logic:
- The method creates a new OpenMapRealVector result by copying this vector.
- It iterates only over the non-zero entries of "this".
- For each non-zero entry in "this" it sets the result entry to the product of this value and the corresponding value in v.
- There is a comment acknowledging a known bug (MATH-803) that the approach assumes zero multiplied by any value (including NaN or infinity) equals zero. But if this[i] == 0 and v[i] is NaN or infinity, this loop misses those cases because it only loops over non-zero entries in "this".
- The comment states these special cases are handled below, but the code snippet ends without any further handling.

The likely cause of failure is that the special cases are not actually handled in the current implementation: the method just returns the result after processing non-zero entries, ignoring positions where "this" is zero but the other vector has NaN or infinity. Because the product in those cases should be NaN or infinity (not zero), the result vector is wrong.

Hence, the defect is in OpenMapRealVector.ebeMultiply method's insufficient handling of entries where "this" is zero and v has NaN or infinity - these cases are not handled as the comment suggests they should be.

The recent bug reports do not seem relevant.

Next, it would be useful to check OpenMapRealVector.ebeDivide to see if it has a similar bug or how it handles these cases. Also, checking if there is a helper function or method dealing with these special element-wise operations might help.

We can also check the full code of the test method (doTestEbeBinaryOperation) to see what it asserts exactly.

I suggest to fetch OpenMapRealVector.ebeDivide and the test helper doTestEbeBinaryOperation for more context.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis  
Details: The test method testEbeMultiplySameType calls doTestEbeBinaryOperation with BinaryOperation.MUL on two vectors of the same implementation. The test builds two vectors of length 100, where entries come from a set of values including normal numbers and special values (NaN, positive and negative infinity). It expects the element-wise multiplication result to exactly equal the product of corresponding entries in arrays data1 and data2.

The bug report and code inspection show that OpenMapRealVector.ebeMultiply iterates only over non-zero entries in "this" vector, multiplying those with the corresponding entry from vector v and setting in result. However, if "this[i]" == 0.0 and v[i] is NaN or infinity, the method does not touch the result at that index, leaving the entry at 0.0 (copied originally), which is incorrect. In mathematical terms 0 * NaN or 0 * infinity is not defined as 0; it results in NaN or infinity respectively.

There is a comment in OpenMapRealVector.ebeMultiply recognizing this problem (MATH-803) and stating these special cases would be handled below, but the implementation does not handle them, simply returning result as is. This causes the test to fail where these corner cases occur.

The ebeDivide method has the same iteration-only-over-nonzero-entries approach, but the comment similarly indicates a potential issue for 0/0, though no extra handling is done either.

The test verifies the exact numeric correctness of every entry, including edge cases involving NaN and infinity, leading to the failure.

Root cause: OpenMapRealVector.ebeMultiply incorrectly handles multiplication where this vector has zeros but the other vector has NaN or infinity values. These cases are not addressed despite comments indicating awareness.

Recommended fix: Implement explicit handling for these special cases by checking all indices or modifying iteration to incorporate these edge cases rather than ignoring zero entries in this vector.

No relevant insights from recent bug reports.

The following methods are recommended for fix or further investigation:
- OpenMapRealVector.ebeMultiply(RealVector)
- OpenMapRealVector.ebeDivide(RealVector) (if similar handling needed)

Optionally:
- test helper method RealVectorAbstractTest.doTestEbeBinaryOperation to understand more test scenarios (already inspected).

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
